question.problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloids $x=5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}$ and the parabolic cylinder $x=9-4{y}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{a(y)}^{b(y)}\,f(y,z)\,dz\,dy
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $yz$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =9-4{y}^{2} \\ 9{y}^{2}+{z}^{2} & =9\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $yz$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type II region: 

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}\le x\le 9-4{y}^{2}\},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse $9{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=9.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}^{9-4{y}^{2}}\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(9-4{y}^{2})-(5{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}},$

for $-1\le y\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}}}^{\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}}}\,9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{9-9{y}^{2}})}^{2}+(9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =(9-9{y}^{2})+(9-9{y}^{2})+(9-9{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}) \\  & =27-27{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
